subject: general
question: Which lake in Himachal Pradesh is associated with Baisakhi celebrations?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rewalsar Lake**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rewalsar Lake** is situated in the **Mandi** district of **Himachal Pradesh** at an altitude of about **1,360 meters** above sea level.
 
• It is a sacred site for three major religions: **Hinduism**, **Buddhism**, and **Sikhism**, making it a unique symbol of religious harmony.
 
• The lake is famously associated with **Baisakhi celebrations**. On this occasion, pilgrims from various regions gather to take a holy dip in the lake, believing it washes away sins. ***Hence, the correct answer is Rewalsar Lake.***
 
• For **Buddhists**, the lake is known as **Tso Pema** (Lotus Lake). It is associated with **Guru Padmasambhava** (also known as **Guru Rinpoche**), who is credited with establishing **Vajrayana Buddhism** in **Tibet**.
 
• The lake features seven islands of floating reed, which are considered sacred. It is believed that the spirit of **Guru Padmasambhava** resides within them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Loktak Lake**:

 
 
• Located in the state of **Manipur**, it is the largest **freshwater lake** in **North-East India**.
 
• It is world-famous for its **phumdis**, which are floating heterogeneous masses of vegetation, soil, and organic matter.
 
• The lake hosts the **Keibul Lamjao National Park**, the only **floating national park** in the world, which is the last natural refuge of the endangered **Sangai** (brow-antlered deer). ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Chilika Lake**:
 
 
• Situated in **Odisha**, it is the largest **brackish water lagoon** in **India** and the second largest in the world.
 
• In **1981**, it was designated as the first **Indian wetland of international importance** under the **Ramsar Convention**.
 
• It is a major wintering ground for **migratory birds** and home to the **Irrawaddy dolphins**. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Pushkar Lake**:
 
 
• Located in the **Ajmer** district of **Rajasthan**, this lake is considered one of the most sacred places for **Hindus**.
 
• It is surrounded by **52 bathing ghats** and over **400 temples**, including the prominent **Brahma Temple**.
 
• The famous **Pushkar Camel Fair** takes place here during the month of **Kartik** (October-November). ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical and Religious Significance:**

 
 
• **Hinduism**: The lake is associated with **Lomas Rishi**, who performed penance here to appease **Lord Shiva**.
 
• **Sikhism**: The **tenth Sikh Guru**, **Guru Gobind Singh**, visited Rewalsar in **1701** to meet with the local hill Rajas to seek their support against the **Mughal Empire**. A **Gurudwara** built in **1930** commemorates his visit.
 
• **Buddhism**: The **Sishu Fair** (also called **Chesu Fair**) is celebrated here annually in the month of **February** or **March** to mark the birth anniversary of **Guru Padmasambhava**.
 
 
 
• **Baisakhi**: It is the **Solar New Year** celebrated across **North India**. In **Himachal Pradesh**, it is also known as **Beesh** or **Bishu** and marks the beginning of the harvesting season.
